a: Iceland is a Nordic island country in the North Atlantic, located just south of the Arctic Circle, with a population of about 390,000 — one of the most sparsely populated countries in Europe. Its capital and largest city is Reykjavik, and its official language is Icelandic, a North Germanic language closely related to Old Norse. Geologically, Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet, making it one of the most volcanically active places on Earth — it has over 30 active volcano systems and is nicknamed the 'Land of Fire and Ice' for its combination of volcanoes and glaciers. Despite its name and latitude, Iceland's climate is moderated by the Gulf Stream, so winters are milder than its name suggests, though it's cool, windy, and changeable year-round. It's also famous for geothermal energy, hot springs, and the northern lights.

a: Brazil is the largest country in South America and the fifth-largest in the world by area, covering about 8.5 million square kilometers. Its population is roughly 215 million, making it the seventh most populous country, and its capital is Brasília, while its largest city is São Paulo. The official language is Portuguese — Brazil is the largest Portuguese-speaking nation in the world — and it's the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas. Brazil is famous for the Amazon rainforest (which contains about 60% of its territory and the majority of the world's remaining rainforest), the Amazon River, Carnival, samba and bossa nova music, football (it has won the World Cup a record five times), and its diverse ecosystems from the Pantanal wetlands to the Atlantic coast. It's the largest economy in Latin America.

a: Japan is an island nation in East Asia consisting of nearly 7,000 islands, with four main islands — Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Shikoku — and a population of about 125 million. Its capital is Tokyo, the most populous metropolitan area in the world, and its currency is the yen. The official language is Japanese, and the country is known for its blend of ancient traditions (Shinto shrines, Buddhist temples, tea ceremony, kimono) and cutting-edge technology, from bullet trains (Shinkansen) to robotics. Japan is a volcanic archipelago with Mount Fuji as its highest peak, and it sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, experiencing frequent earthquakes. It's famous for anime, manga, sushi and ramen, cherry blossom season, and a highly developed economy that is the fourth largest in the world.

a: India is a country in South Asia and the most populous country in the world, with over 1.4 billion people. Its capital is New Delhi, and it has no single national language — Hindi and English are the official languages of the central government, but the country recognizes 22 scheduled languages and speaks hundreds more. India is the birthplace of four major religions: Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism; roughly 80% of Indians are Hindu, with significant Muslim, Christian, Sikh, and Buddhist minorities. Geographically it spans the Himalayas in the north to tropical coasts in the south, with the Ganges River as a sacred lifeline. India is known for its ancient civilizations, Bollywood cinema, cricket, yoga, curry and spices, the Taj Mahal, and its rapidly growing technology sector. It gained independence from British rule in 1947.

a: France is a country in Western Europe with a population of about 68 million, and its capital is Paris, one of the world's great cultural centers. The official language is French, and the currency is the euro. France is the largest country in the EU by area, bordered by the Atlantic Ocean, the Mediterranean Sea, and six other countries, and its landscape ranges from the Alps and Pyrenees mountains to the Normandy coast and the vineyards of Bordeaux and Burgundy. It's renowned for its art and architecture (the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower, Versailles), its cuisine (bread, cheese, wine), its history of revolution and republics, and as the birthplace of cinema and Impressionism. France is a founding member of the European Union and the UN Security Council, and it was the most-visited country in the world before the pandemic.
